subject: Chemistry
topic: Physical properties of aldehydes and ketones
title: Same Weight, 0 °C vs 97 °C: Physical Properties of Aldehydes and Ketones
summary: Five compounds of the same mass boil from 0 °C to 97 °C. Aldehydes and ketones sit in the middle: their polar C=O gives dipole-dipole attraction, but with no O–H they cannot hydrogen-bond with each other. Water can hydrogen-bond to the C=O oxygen, so small aldehydes and ketones mix with water while long chains do not.

notes.title: 05 – Physical Properties of Aldehydes and Ketones

keyPoints: Same molar mass (58–60): **butane 0 °C < methoxyethane 8 °C < propanal 49 °C < acetone 56 °C < propan-1-ol 97 °C** (NCERT 8.3).
The C=O is **polar** (C δ+, O δ−): neighbouring molecules attract **dipole to dipole**, so aldehydes and ketones boil above hydrocarbons and ethers.
No **O–H**, so no hydrogen bonds between their own molecules: they boil **below alcohols** of similar mass.
Water's H **hydrogen-bonds to the carbonyl O**: methanal, ethanal and propanone mix in all proportions; **longer chains are less soluble**.

head: Property
What to remember
rows: methanal gas; ethanal volatile liquid; others liquids or solids
lower aldehydes pungent; larger ones fragrant (perfumes, flavours)
small ones mix in all proportions (H-bonds to C=O); solubility falls as the chain grows
all dissolve in benzene, ether, methanol, chloroform

quiz.q: Of these (similar mass), which boils highest?
Aldehydes boil higher than alkanes of similar mass because of:
quiz.explain: The polar C=O attracts neighbouring C=O groups.

quiz.q: Aldehydes cannot hydrogen-bond with each other because they have no:
quiz.explain: No H on oxygen to donate.

quiz.q: Which mixes with water in all proportions?
quiz.explain: Small carbonyls H-bond with water through the C=O oxygen.
